top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P002) is my first choice on the common criteria of voice, formal achievement, sustained quality and imaginative depth. As publicly described, Blinding and Solenoid form one sustained construction of dense sentences, the interior body and city, and dream cosmology. His poetry and prose together make a long oeuvre, and the recent novels appear to have kept their ambition. This is the claim I can state most plainly as one about language and construction on the page. It does not rest on nationality, fame or political symbolism, and shared support from Mattson is not evidence of merit. Carson (P001) is a close second. The narrowed citation to original written work (verse novel, lyric, elegy, essays) answers my earlier scope objection about hybrid and book-object forms. What remains open for her is whether the mid-career and later books sustain the level of Autobiography of Red and Nox. For Cărtărescu the open question is whether the recurring motifs are development or repetition. I judge him through translation and public knowledge only, and I have not verified the corpus. My confidence is moderate, and a volume-by-volume reading or an expert reading of the Romanian could change the order. Both proposals are literarily serious and rank above no award (P000), which I rank last.
recusal_note: None apparent from the profile. It records no personal, institutional or professional connection to Cărtărescu, Carson or any other shortlisted writer. I disclose a thematic proximity between my own documentary historical fiction and Central and Eastern European settings, and between my years in Prague and Vienna and Cărtărescu's Romanian context. I treat this as context, not as evidence of preference. Conflicts are disclosed and not adjudicated in this simulation.
